headline: Adds a health-check web address that reports the app is running and its version number, with no effect on parcel lookups.
what_changed: The app now answers a new address, /healthz, that the load balancer (the traffic splitter in front of the servers) can check.
When the app is running, that address replies that it is OK and shows the version number, currently 4.1.2.
Customers and parcel tracking work the same as before. Nothing about orders, parcels or customer data changes.
A matching automatic test was added, and the setup notes in the README now list the new address.

risks.title: Health check says OK even if parcel lookups are broken
risks.explanation: The new address only confirms that the server responds. It does not check whether parcel lookups work. The load balancer could keep sending traffic to a server that is up but failing at real work. This is normal for simple health checks, so it is a limit to know about rather than a fault. If you want a deeper check, ask a developer to test a real lookup inside the check.

risks.title: Version number is visible to anyone
risks.explanation: Anyone who visits the new address can see the app's version number. Knowing the exact version can help an attacker look for known weaknesses in that version. The risk is small because it reveals nothing about customer data, but a developer could drop the version from the public reply if you prefer.

questions_for_developer: Does the publishing process include the package.json file? The app reads its version number from that file at startup, so the app would fail to start if the file is left out.
Should the health check also confirm that parcel lookups work, or is a simple 'server is running' check enough for the load balancer?
Is it fine for anyone on the internet to see the version number at this address, or should it be limited to the load balancer?
good_news: The change is small and separate from the existing parcel lookup code.
The version number comes from the same file the app already uses, so it stays in step with the release number.
A new automatic test checks that the address answers correctly.
